bug_semantics: Access-rule authorization compared raw virtual paths as case-sensitive, slash-separated strings, while the host filesystem resolved equivalent names using its own case and separator semantics. On case-insensitive filesystems, a case variant of a denied path therefore missed the rule but reached the same file; on Windows, backslashes and traversal components likewise missed slash-based rules but were normalized by the filesystem. An authenticated user could consequently read or, subject to ordinary permissions, mutate an administrator-denied file while remaining inside the user's filesystem scope.
flaw_origin: Commit 9c36dea485ddd16a90f0a615e20baddaee6b9cde is the smallest real origin in the lineage that became File Browser v2. It added User.Allowed with the raw literal comparison strings.HasPrefix(url, rule.Path) and added HTTP handlers that passed request-derived paths to Allowed before filesystem access. Its sole parent 780f1bc16e4e5270fed2a6b7da442a47084d8c4b has no Rule type, User.Allowed function, or vulnerable comparison. The earlier 20baeeb41a9555cefc3b31b495e24e907736c443 was a 10,626-line bulk import explicitly described as based on caddy-filemanager and was removed during the rewrite, so it is rejected as an import rather than selected as the BIC. Later commits moved or extracted the same mechanism, and public master received it in squash aggregate 12b2c215221696de58431093e01eeff7a5414471.
ai_marker: absent: raw BIC commit object 9c36dea485ddd16a90f0a615e20baddaee6b9cde names Henrique Dias <hacdias@gmail.com> as both author and committer, has message 'updates', and contains only ordinary metadata plus a PGP signature; it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, AI trailer, or other AI signal
evidence: The first-party advisory https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/security/advisories/GHSA-fgm5-pw99-w2p7 identifies rules.Rule.Matches and data.Check, describes case-variant and Windows-separator path equivalence, states affected versions <=2.63.20 and patched version v2.63.21, and names PR #6045. For the introducer disagreement, the primary selected 9c36dea485ddd16a90f0a615e20baddaee6b9cde with parent 780f1bc16e4e5270fed2a6b7da442a47084d8c4b, while the reviewer selected 3dcbdfc8776b25f58a9134ba9f4d893f62db2b7c with parent 8e6e2119db14d33b56fc2dff13e0cf7c99439438. Fresh `git ls-remote ... refs/pull/575/head` resolved the surviving PR head to a23f868abb77e53a5bca92022464dab2da7b756c. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 9c36... a23f...` succeeded, whereas the same command for 3dcb... failed. Starting from that surviving head, chained `git log -L` checks on rules/rules.go:Matches, types/rule.go:isAllowed, types/user.go:IsAllowed, lib/filebrowser.go:Allowed, user.go:Allowed, and filemanager.go:Allowed followed the same literal matcher backward through 6811f205b43414fe74d1a9fbbb28e54f3318ff55, 9adb60206c0cfd1592eada3955d4e87bc2edf27c, 42227d9edd7ce613e8b6c0ad62c8cad16cf77266, 5b619337df9e9dd04e47d9c2da29a92c31adfed3, and 174330929ad7231b95b30acb98ad2033d697590f to its addition in 9c36dea485ddd16a90f0a615e20baddaee6b9cde. `git show 9c36... -- filemanager.go http.go` shows that BIC adding both raw `strings.HasPrefix(url, rule.Path)` authorization and request-to-filesystem enforcement. `git cat-file -p 9c36...` identifies sole parent 780f1bc16e4e5270fed2a6b7da442a47084d8c4b, and `git grep -n -E 'func \(u User\) Allowed|HasPrefix\(url, rule.Path\)|type Rule struct' 780f... -- '*.go'` returned no matches. The reviewer's 3dcb... is a re-creation in a superseded force-push history, not an ancestor of the surviving PR head, and therefore is rejected as a rewrite rather than the smallest source origin. Public aggregate 12b2c215221696de58431093e01eeff7a5414471 says `feat: v2 (#599)` and points to PR #575; `git describe --contains --tags 12b2...` returned `v2.0.0-rc.1~42`, establishing that the carried flaw predates the v2 line. For the fix disagreement, both audits' core fix_sha e6d70cf24c0cd79a1787601dc99104ec7e7ca3ef is confirmed: its diff canonicalizes paths before rule decisions and folds non-regex path rules on case-insensitive filesystems. `git describe --contains --tags e6d70...` returned `v2.63.21~1`; ancestry succeeds for v2.63.21 and fails for v2.63.20; the v2.63.21 release commit f6fb8f6bf52d714b2215534033a3c96316069efc has e6d70... as its immediate parent. The primary/reviewer differed on the direct fix: fresh `git ls-remote ... refs/pull/6045/head` returned 4bc6aca02f0ef8db01f200ed39027ffc2e9d9ddb, and stable patch-id for 4bc6... and landed e6d70... was identically 655bbf034ee48ad20ed4de520197608a3296f7db, so direct_fix_sha is 4bc6... while fix_sha is e6d70.... For marker_state, raw `git cat-file -p 9c36...` showed human author/committer metadata, a PGP signature, message `updates`, and no AI marker; the primary's explicit absent state wins over the reviewer's null.
reasoning: The authorization/filesystem path-equivalence mismatch is the vulnerability, so the BIC must be the first non-import commit that wrote that matcher together with a path reaching filesystem operations. The surviving PR #575 lineage, rather than an abandoned force-push rewrite, is the relevant decomposition of the public v2 squash. Its line history reaches 9c36dea485ddd16a90f0a615e20baddaee6b9cde, and the direct parent proves absence, so the primary is correct on introducer_sha and introducer_parent; the reviewer was wrong to treat 3dcbdfc8776b25f58a9134ba9f4d893f62db2b7c's later rewrite as the source origin. The advisory and tag ancestry independently close the version boundary at vulnerable v2.63.20 and fixed v2.63.21. Both audits named the correct landed fix e6d70cf24c0cd79a1787601dc99104ec7e7ca3ef, but the primary correctly distinguished PR head 4bc6aca02f0ef8db01f200ed39027ffc2e9d9ddb as direct_fix_sha. Attribution uses only the verified BIC commit object: it contains no AI signal, so marker_state is explicitly absent rather than unknown/null and the gate-complete verdict is NOT_AI.
